title: Indistractable: How to Control Your Attention and Choose Your Life
author: Nir Eyal with Julie Li
target_audience: Professionals aiming to improve focus and productivity
Students struggling with distractions and time management
Anyone seeking strategies for self-control and habit change
core_themes: Living intentionally according to one's values
primary_purpose: To empower readers to take back control of their attention by understanding the psychological triggers of distraction and applying evidence-based techniques to live more intentionally and productively.

structure_format.organization: Four parts outlining the model: mastering internal triggers, making time for traction, hacking back external triggers, preventing distraction, plus sections for parenting and relationships

key_concepts_lessons: Distraction is often a response to discomfort or internal triggers; managing these triggers is essential.
The opposite of distraction is ‘traction’—actions that pull you toward your values and goals.
Time management is pain management—addressing the root causes of distraction is essential.
Schedule your values: time-boxing ensures you align actions with intentions.
External triggers, such as notifications, can be managed and ‘hacked back’ for better focus.
Making precommitments and setting up pacts strengthens your ability to resist distractions.
Being ‘indistractable’ is a lifelong practice requiring ongoing assessment and adjustment.
notable_features: Provides scripts for workplace and family discussions
Includes digital detox advice without advocating total abstinence
Emphasizes systems and identity-change over willpower alone
cultural_historical_context: Published during an era of rising concerns over smartphone usage, social media addiction, and information overload, reflecting societal struggles with focus and well-being in the digital age.
reception_impact: Acclaimed by productivity and self-help circles for practical, science-backed advice
Frequently recommended by business leaders and educators
Praised for its actionable tips and clear frameworks; some critics note overlap with existing habit literature
Led to workshops and resources for individuals and businesses
comparable_titles: The Power of Habit by Charles Duhigg
